---
title: "About"
---

I'm a data scientist with over a decade in industry, based in Berlin. Most of it has been forecasting and
recommender systems in production — measuring systems whose output is stochastic, where the metric is
easy to compute and what it licenses you to say is not.

This site is where I write up work on **LLM evaluation and measurement validity**: what an eval harness
can actually control, where a benchmark's number stops carrying information, and how to tell those
apart. The recurring theme is that agentic evals make implicit claims about what a model had access to,
and those claims are properties of the harness rather than of the task.

## Things I've done in the open

- **A merged contribution to [`inspect_ai`](https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai)**, the
  eval framework maintained by the UK AI Security Institute
  ([PR #4913](https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai/pull/4913)), plus an open question on
  whether runtime filtering of tool outputs is in scope
  ([#5020](https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai/issues/5020)).
- **[Notes on filtering tool outputs in Inspect](posts/filtering-tool-outputs-in-inspect.qmd)** —
  where the framework can and cannot intercept a tool response, and a hook that fails open silently.
- Ongoing: measuring whether published agentic-safety evals still discriminate on current models —
  replication first, write-up only if the numbers hold up.
